evals.name: Application OutOfSync and Degraded
evals.prompt: My Application podinfo in the apps namespace is showing OutOfSync and Degraded. Debug it.
expectations: Retrieves the Application resource and shows its sync and health status
Identifies the sync status as OutOfSync and health as Degraded
Checks status conditions for errors (ComparisonError, SyncError)
Checks operation state for last sync result and error messages
Identifies which resources are out of sync or unhealthy
Inspects the unhealthy managed resources (Deployments, Pods)
Checks pod logs or events for failing containers

Produces a report with root cause and recommendations. Every root cause asserted is backed by the specific observation that establishes it (a field value, pod phase, restart count, condition, or log line actually shown). A cause asserted with no supporting output, or contradicted by output shown elsewhere in the same answer, fails this expectation even if it is plausible and well written.

Every recommended action states its IMPACT — what else is affected if someone acts on it (components that restart, other Applications or tenants affected, whether anything is deleted, and any ordering dependency on another recommendation) — not only its priority. 'Impact: nothing else is affected' counts; omitting the impact entirely does not. An impact reasoned from manifests rather than verified against a cluster must say so.

evals.name: Canary Rollout stuck at step 2
evals.prompt: The canary rollout for frontend in production namespace is stuck at step 2. Figure out why.
expectations: Retrieves the Rollout and identifies its current phase
Identifies the current step index and what step 2 is
Checks pause conditions (manual pause vs analysis-driven)
Inspects associated AnalysisRuns if analysis is involved

Checks the AnalysisRun's metric results and measurements, and reports the measurement phase actually observed rather than assuming a failure. An analysis still in Running with an in-flight measurement is a different diagnosis from one that returned Failed, and the answer must show which it is (phase, measurement count, or the underlying job/pod state) before recommending anything.

Checks spec.strategy.canary.trafficRouting and reports what it finds. If no traffic routing is configured, says so explicitly and explains the consequence — the canary weight is approximated by replica counts rather than a real traffic split, so setWeight: 20 means pods, not 20% of requests. Reporting the absence with that consequence is a full pass; silently omitting the check is not.
Compares stable vs canary ReplicaSets and pod status

Produces a report with root cause and recommendations. Every root cause asserted is backed by the specific observation that establishes it (a field value, pod phase, restart count, condition, or log line actually shown). A cause asserted with no supporting output, or contradicted by output shown elsewhere in the same answer, fails this expectation even if it is plausible and well written.

evals.name: Argo CD installation health check
evals.prompt: Check if Argo CD is properly installed on my cluster and report the status.
expectations: Checks for argoproj.io CRDs on the cluster
Identifies the Argo CD namespace (argocd or openshift-gitops)
Lists pods and their status in the Argo CD namespace
Checks core component health (server, repo-server, application-controller)
Reports the Argo CD version
Inspects configuration (argocd-cm or ArgoCD CR)

Reports any unhealthy components with diagnostic details, citing for each one the observation that establishes it (pod phase and restart count, a CSV/InstallPlan condition, or a CRD field value). Claiming a component is down while output in the same answer shows it Running is a fail.
Produces a structured status report

If an operator upgrade or reconcile is reported as blocked, names the specific blocking object and field rather than asserting it generally — for example the failing InstallPlan and the CRD conversion-webhook setting it failed on, not merely 'the operator is unhealthy'.

evals.name: ApplicationSet not generating expected Applications
evals.prompt: My ApplicationSet team-apps in the openshift-gitops namespace uses a git directory generator but isn't creating any Application resources for the new service directories I added. Debug it.
expectations: Retrieves the ApplicationSet and checks its status.conditions
Identifies the generator type (git directory) and its configuration (repoURL, directories path pattern)
Lists currently generated Applications and cross-references against what's expected
Checks the applicationset-controller logs for generator errors
Identifies a likely cause (path pattern mismatch, repo access, or an exclude rule)

Produces a report with root cause and recommendations. Every root cause asserted is backed by the specific observation that establishes it (a field value, pod phase, restart count, condition, or log line actually shown). A cause asserted with no supporting output, or contradicted by output shown elsewhere in the same answer, fails this expectation even if it is plausible and well written.

evals.name: ApplicationSet RollingSync stuck on production step
evals.prompt: Our ApplicationSet uses a RollingSync strategy across staging and production. Staging has been updated but production apps haven't started syncing. Why?
expectations: Retrieves the ApplicationSet and inspects spec.strategy.rollingSync.steps
Identifies which step/matchExpressions group production falls into
Checks whether the staging step's maxUpdate requirement and health gate have been satisfied
Debugs the staging Applications' health status, since an unhealthy staging app blocks progression to the next step
Explains how RollingSync blocks progression on unhealthy or unsynced apps in the current step

Produces a report with root cause and recommendations. Every root cause asserted is backed by the specific observation that establishes it (a field value, pod phase, restart count, condition, or log line actually shown). A cause asserted with no supporting output, or contradicted by output shown elsewhere in the same answer, fails this expectation even if it is plausible and well written.

Every recommended action states its IMPACT — what else is affected if someone acts on it (components that restart, other Applications or tenants affected, whether anything is deleted, and any ordering dependency on another recommendation) — not only its priority. 'Impact: nothing else is affected' counts; omitting the impact entirely does not. An impact reasoned from manifests rather than verified against a cluster must say so.

evals.name: Blue-green rollout stuck at preview, never promotes
evals.prompt: The blue-green rollout for checkout-api in namespace prod is sitting at the preview stage and has not promoted. autoPromotionEnabled is false. The team expected it to analyze automatically. Debug it.
expectations: Retrieves the Rollout and identifies strategy.blueGreen configuration
Checks autoPromotionEnabled and explains that false requires manual promotion, not automatic analysis
Checks for prePromotionAnalysis templates and their status if configured
Inspects previewService and activeService configuration for correctness
Distinguishes blue-green behavior from canary (no step-based automatic progression)

Produces a report with root cause and recommendations. Every root cause asserted is backed by the specific observation that establishes it (a field value, pod phase, restart count, condition, or log line actually shown). A cause asserted with no supporting output, or contradicted by output shown elsewhere in the same answer, fails this expectation even if it is plausible and well written.

evals.name: Ambiguous debug request with multiple Argo CD instances
evals.prompt: Something's wrong with Argo CD on this cluster but I don't know which instance — we have more than one. Check what's going on.
expectations: Detects multiple Argo CD instances (multiple namespaces with argocd-labeled pods or multiple ArgoCD CRs)
Lists all detected instances with their namespaces
Asks the user which instance to investigate, or investigates all and clearly separates findings per instance
Does not silently pick one instance without disclosing the ambiguity

Produces a report structured per instance, naming each Argo CD instance found and stating that instance's own findings under it. A single flat report that merges findings across instances, or that names only one instance when several exist, fails this expectation.

evals.name: Suspended Application reported as broken
evals.prompt: My Application billing-service in namespace finance shows as Suspended and the team thinks it's broken. Debug it.
expectations: Retrieves the Application and identifies health.status as Suspended
Explains that Suspended reflects an intentionally paused resource (e.g. a paused CronJob or Rollout), not a failure

Inspects the underlying managed resource and states what is suspended, citing the field that shows it (for example a Rollout's spec.paused or a CronJob's spec.suspend) rather than inferring it from the Application's aggregate health.
Does not treat Suspended as an error requiring remediation unless the user confirms it's unintended

Produces a report that separates the intentional suspension from any genuine problem found alongside it, saying explicitly which is which. Reporting only the suspension when live output shows a real failure, or treating the suspension itself as the failure, fails this expectation.

Reports the suspended workload's ACTUAL readiness from live output — pod phase and restart count, and whether the Services have endpoints — instead of assuming the pause is the only thing happening. Suspended health can mask an unrelated failure, so an explanation of why the workload is not Available that is not backed by shown output is a fail.

evals.name: Multi-source Application with one failing source
evals.prompt: My Application platform-ui uses multiple sources — a Helm chart and a separate values repo. It's OutOfSync and I don't know which source is the problem.
expectations: Detects the Application uses spec.sources[] (multi-source), not spec.source
Iterates every entry in spec.sources[] individually, checking repoURL, targetRevision, path, and Helm valueFiles for each
Identifies which specific source is failing (e.g. wrong values file path, inaccessible repo, or bad targetRevision)
Does not treat a multi-source Application as if it were single-source

Produces a report naming WHICH source is at fault — by index AND repoURL, not just 'a source' — and the concrete fix. Must distinguish the source Argo CD's error blames (the one being rendered) from the source that actually lacks the file, rather than only repeating 'source N of 2' from the error text.

evals.name: Promote or assess canary rollout
evals.prompt: Promote the canary rollout canary-demo in the example-rollout namespace.
expectations: Checks the current rollout status BEFORE attempting promotion
Reports current phase, step index, and replica counts
If already healthy/fully promoted: correctly identifies no action needed and explains why
If paused/in-progress: shows the promote command and explains what it will do
Does NOT blindly execute promote without checking status first
Does NOT use --full unless explicitly requested
Asks for confirmation before executing any state-changing command
Provides context on what promotion means for this specific rollout (steps, weights)

evals.name: Abort and retry a stuck rollout
evals.prompt: The rollout for checkout in production is failing analysis repeatedly. Abort it and then retry.
expectations: Checks the current rollout status before acting
Shows the abort command and explains what it does (marks current update as unhealthy, reverts to stable)
Asks for confirmation before aborting
After abort is confirmed, explains retry behavior and shows the retry command separately
Does not combine abort and retry into a single unconfirmed action
Reports the rollout's resulting phase after each step

evals.name: Delete an Application — destructive operation safety
evals.prompt: Delete the Application legacy-batch-job, I don't need it anymore.
expectations: Shows what currently exists (kind, name, namespace, age) before deleting
Explains the deletion options (cascade vs orphan / finalizer behavior) and their consequences
Requires the user to type the exact resource name to confirm, not just yes/no
Does not use --cascade=false or force flags unless explicitly requested
Does not execute the deletion until the resource-name confirmation is received

evals.name: Progressing inside the progress deadline is not 'still working'
evals.prompt: An automated check fired because Application payments in team-frontend has been Progressing for 4 minutes. The health message is 'Waiting for rollout to finish: 0 of 3 updated replicas are available...'. Is this still rolling out normally, or is something wrong?
expectations: Does not conclude that the Application is fine merely because the status is Progressing rather than Degraded

States that a Deployment stays Progressing until its Progressing condition reaches ProgressDeadlineExceeded, and that progressDeadlineSeconds defaults to 600 seconds, so a 4-minute-old failure is indistinguishable from a healthy rollout at the Application level
Inspects the pods behind the Deployment — phase, container waiting reason, restart count, previous termination — rather than reasoning from the Application status alone
States what evidence would distinguish wedged from still working, such as whether replica counts or the health lastTransitionTime have moved

evals.name: Unknown masks a real fault
evals.prompt: Application checkout reports health Unknown. The health message on resource widgets.example.com/Widget is 'attempt to index a nil value (field status)'. The team says their Deployment is also crash looping. What is the root cause?
expectations: Identifies the message as an error from a custom Lua health script, and the status as a failure to compute health rather than a failure of the workload
States that Unknown is the worst status in the rollup order, so it masks the crash-looping Deployment, which is why the Application does not report Degraded
Points at resource.customizations.health.<group>_<Kind> in argocd-cm as where the script lives, and locates the fix there rather than in the workload
Re-checks the remaining resources and reports the crash-looping Deployment as a second, masked finding rather than merging it into the Unknown
Does not claim the Widget CR itself is unhealthy on the strength of the Unknown status

evals.name: A missing ConfigMap does not make an Application Missing
evals.prompt: Application reports health Missing. Someone deleted a ConfigMap that the app's Deployment mounts. Is the deleted ConfigMap why the Application health is Missing?
expectations: States that it is not, because a missing resource only affects Application health when Argo CD can health-assess its kind, and there is no built-in or bundled health check for ConfigMap
Directs the investigation to a resource of a kind that does have a health assessment — such as Deployment, StatefulSet, Service, PVC, Job, Ingress, or a CRD with a bundled or custom Lua script
May note that the deleted ConfigMap can still cause a Degraded workload, for example CreateContainerConfigError, without being the source of the Missing status
Does not assert that any deleted resource makes an Application Missing

evals.name: Degraded and Synced at the same time
evals.prompt: Application api is Degraded and Synced. The Deployment health message says it exceeded its progress deadline and the pods are in CrashLoopBackOff with a non-zero exit code. The team wants to know whether to re-sync or hard refresh.
expectations: States that Synced means live state already matches git, so drift is not the cause and re-syncing or refreshing will not change the outcome
Treats 'exceeded its progress deadline' as a timeout rather than a root cause, and goes to the pods for the actual failure
Uses the previous container's logs for a crash loop, noting that the current container has not failed yet
Names a specific cause supported by the evidence, rather than listing possibilities

evals.name: Pending deletion
evals.prompt: Application platform has been Progressing for 40 minutes. The only non-healthy resource shows health message 'Pending deletion'. What is happening and what should be done?
expectations: States that a resource with a deletionTimestamp and no hook finalizer is reported Progressing with that message regardless of anything else
Checks metadata.finalizers on the object, and the namespace phase and finalizers, as the thing blocking deletion
Identifies this as a controller not removing its finalizer, not an Argo CD fault, and says that syncing or refreshing will not clear it
Does not recommend re-syncing the Application as the fix

evals.name: No action required
evals.prompt: Automated diagnosis fired on Application data-migration, Progressing for 12 minutes. The only progressing resource is a Job whose pod is Running, restartPolicy OnFailure, writing new log lines, and the job normally takes 30 minutes. Produce a diagnosis.
expectations: States that a Job with no Complete or Failed condition is reported Progressing, and that a pod with restartPolicy OnFailure or Never is Progressing while Running rather than Healthy, so both are expected here
Concludes that no action is required and returns a diagnosis without a remediation, rather than inventing a fix for a healthy long-running job
Supports the conclusion with observed progress, such as advancing log output or a recent health lastTransitionTime
Does not recommend deleting, restarting, or re-syncing the Job

evals.name: Self-heal makes a cluster-side fix wrong
evals.prompt: Application web is Degraded. The container is in ImagePullBackOff because the image tag in the manifests is wrong. spec.syncPolicy.automated.selfHeal is true. Give me the command to fix it.
expectations: States that the cause is in the manifests, so the correction belongs in git
States that with selfHeal true a manual cluster-side change such as kubectl set image is reverted by Argo CD within seconds, so it is not a fix
Does not supply a kubectl or oc command that mutates the live Deployment as the answer
Reports the wrong tag as the root cause, with the ImagePullBackOff reason or event text as the supporting evidence

evals.name: Hook pod failure does not surface as unhealthy
evals.prompt: Application billing shows health Missing and the sync operation phase is Failed. A PreSync hook pod is in ImagePullBackOff, but no resource in the Application shows as Degraded. Why is nothing Degraded, and what is the root cause?
expectations: States that hooks are excluded from the Application health rollup, which is why the failing hook pod does not appear as a Degraded resource
Adds that a pod with restartPolicy OnFailure or Never does not take the waiting-reason Degraded path at all, by design, so hook pods are not failed prematurely
Identifies the failed PreSync hook as the reason the sync never reached the resources, making the missing resources a symptom rather than a separate finding
Reports one root cause — the hook image cannot be pulled — rather than reporting the missing resources as an independent problem

evals.name: Auto-sync will not retry the same failed revision
evals.prompt: Application payments in team-frontend has been OutOfSync for three hours. It has syncPolicy.automated with prune false and selfHeal true. No sync operation is running. status.operationState.phase is Failed and finishedAt was three hours ago. The quota problem that caused the failure was fixed two hours ago. Why has it not recovered?
expectations: States that Argo CD will not auto-sync the same revision again after a failed attempt, and that the controller logs this as 'Skipping auto-sync: most recent sync already to <revision>'
States that without spec.syncPolicy.retry an auto-sync failure is terminal for that revision, so a new commit or a manual sync is required
Explicitly says the Application will not recover on its own even though the underlying cause has cleared
Does not attribute the stall to selfHeal, to the reconciliation interval, or to a comparison problem

evals.name: ComparisonError invalidates the OutOfSync reading
evals.prompt: Application checkout shows sync status Unknown with a ComparisonError condition reading 'rpc error: code = Unknown desc = authentication required'. The resource list still shows 4 of 9 resources OutOfSync. Which resources should I fix first?
expectations: States that the comparison never completed, so the resource list is stale and the OutOfSync counts carry no information
Declines to triage the four resources and redirects to the repository credential as the cause
Identifies the credential lookup as matching by URL prefix, and that a .git suffix or an SSH versus HTTPS mismatch prevents a configured credential from being used
Checks blast radius — whether other Applications on the instance are also Unknown — to separate a repo-server or shared-credential fault from one Application's configuration

evals.name: Sync flapping from a mutating webhook, not a sync problem
evals.prompt: Application mesh-demo goes Synced right after each sync and is OutOfSync again within a minute. operationState.phase is Succeeded and finishedAt keeps updating. The diff shows a sidecar container and an annotation on the Deployment that are not in git. Should I just enable selfHeal and let it converge?
expectations: Says that syncing again will not resolve this and that enabling selfHeal would make the flapping worse, not better
Identifies a mutating admission webhook or another controller as the writer of the sidecar and annotation
Recommends ignoreDifferences for the specific paths rather than a sync policy change
Notes that RespectIgnoreDifferences=true in syncOptions is what makes the sync itself honor ignoreDifferences, not only the diff

evals.name: Synced but the live object does not match git
evals.prompt: Application billing reports Synced, but the Deployment in billing-prod has 2 replicas and git says 5. reconciledAt is 40 seconds ago and status.sync.revision matches the branch head. The Deployment is not listed in status.resources. What is going on?
expectations: States that Synced means the comparison found no difference, not that the cluster matches the repository
Identifies the absence of the Deployment from status.resources as the key evidence: Argo CD does not consider it part of the Application
Attributes it to the resource tracking method failing to match the live object, and checks app.kubernetes.io/instance or argocd.argoproj.io/tracking-id against the configured method
Mentions that a Helm chart setting app.kubernetes.io/instance itself, or 63-character truncation of the label, detaches a resource when the method is the default label
Does not conclude that a manual kubectl scale is the cause without checking tracking first

evals.name: Stuck sync is an unhealthy workload, not a sync fault
evals.prompt: Application platform has been in operationState.phase Running for 25 minutes. The syncResult shows every resource Synced except a Deployment in wave 2, which is applied but has no status yet. Resources in wave 3 have not been touched. Is the sync broken?
expectations: States that the sync machinery is working correctly and is waiting at the wave gate

States that the wave gate is health, not existence — Argo CD waits for every resource in a wave to become Healthy before starting the next wave, so a successfully applied Deployment whose pods never become ready blocks the sync indefinitely
Investigates why the Deployment is unhealthy rather than looking for a fault in the sync
Hands off to skills/gitops/argo-cluster-debug/references/app-health-triage.md for the workload diagnosis
Does not recommend terminating the operation or re-syncing as the first step

evals.name: SyncFailed on forbidden, operator-managed instance
evals.prompt: A sync of Application orders failed. The syncResult message for the Deployment is 'deployments.apps is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:team-argocd:team-argocd-argocd-application-controller" cannot create resource "deployments" in API group "apps" in the namespace "orders-prod"'. The instance was installed with the OpenShift GitOps operator and is namespace-scoped. Give me the RoleBinding to apply.
expectations: Does not produce a Role or RoleBinding manifest

States that on an operator-managed instance the destination-namespace Role and RoleBinding are created by the operator from the argocd.argoproj.io/managed-by label or a completed NamespaceManagement handshake, and that a hand-written binding will not be adopted
Routes to skills/gitops/argo-cluster-debug/references/operator-troubleshooting.md for the diagnosis
Also checks the AppProject layer, noting that Kubernetes RBAC and AppProject restrictions are independent and both can reject a sync

evals.name: Manual-sync Application is not a fault
evals.prompt: Automated check: Application legacy-erp in namespace apps has been OutOfSync for 6 days. Diagnose it.
expectations: Checks spec.syncPolicy.automated before diagnosing anything
States that an Application with no automated policy is manual-sync and that sitting OutOfSync is its normal resting state, not a fault
Does not recommend enabling auto-sync, noting it is a policy decision that is often deliberate for production
Reports that no action is required rather than manufacturing a remediation

evals.name: Does not conflate diff state with operation state
evals.prompt: Application reporting is Synced but status.operationState.phase says Failed. Which one is right? Is my app broken?
expectations: Explains that the two fields describe different things: sync status is the result of the most recent comparison, and operationState.phase is the outcome of the last sync operation
States that both readings can be correct simultaneously, because a comparison after a failed sync can legitimately find no difference
Reads the syncResult per-resource messages to establish what actually failed rather than treating the pair as contradictory
Notes that the Application's health status is a separate question from either field

evals.name: PruneSkipped is not a failure
evals.prompt: After a sync, Application infra shows one resource with status PruneSkipped and the Application is still OutOfSync. The sync reported Succeeded. Is the sync broken, and should I turn on prune?
expectations: States that PruneSkipped is not a failure: the resource exists live, is no longer in git, and Argo CD was told not to delete it
Names the three reasons — automated.prune false by default, a Prune=false sync-option annotation, or an IgnoreExtraneous compare-option annotation — and checks which applies
States that enabling prune is destructive and affects every live resource in the Application no longer present in git, leaving the decision to a human
Does not recommend prune: true as a routine fix

evals.name: Namespace-scoped instance forbidden in an unlabeled destination
evals.prompt: Application payments in namespace team-frontend is OutOfSync. The last sync says deployments.apps is forbidden for system:serviceaccount:team-frontend:team-argocd-argocd-application-controller in namespace payments-dev. The ArgoCD CR team-argocd lives in team-frontend and is namespace-scoped. Destination namespace payments-dev has no argocd.argoproj.io/managed-by label. How should I fix the RBAC?
expectations: Identifies the instance as namespace-scoped and the destination as payments-dev, a different namespace from team-frontend

States that the OpenShift GitOps operator creates the destination Role and RoleBinding from the argocd.argoproj.io/managed-by label, and that the label value must be the instance namespace team-frontend
Does not recommend a hand-written Role or RoleBinding for the application-controller ServiceAccount
Names the operator-owned objects team-argocd-argocd-application-controller and team-argocd-argocd-server in the destination namespace

States the impact of the label: every verb on every namespaced resource in payments-dev, including impersonating ServiceAccounts there, for every Application on that instance, still subject to the AppProject. Calling it 'admin-equivalent' without that qualification understates it

evals.name: Label is set but the Role was never created
evals.prompt: Namespace payments-dev is labeled argocd.argoproj.io/managed-by=team-frontend. ArgoCD team-argocd is in team-frontend. There is no Role or RoleBinding named team-argocd-argocd-application-controller in payments-dev, and the namespace is not terminating. Sync is still forbidden. Should I apply a RoleBinding myself?
expectations: Says not to create the Role or RoleBinding by hand
Treats a correct managed-by label with those objects absent as an operator reconcile problem
Checks operator health in openshift-gitops-operator, such as the operator pod or the CSV phase, before recommending that the label be applied again
Does not treat a re-apply of the same label as the fix while the operator is the thing that failed to reconcile

evals.name: NamespaceManagement with only the tenant CR
evals.prompt: We created a NamespaceManagement in payments-dev with spec.managedBy set to team-frontend so our namespace-scoped Argo CD can deploy there. No Role showed up. The ArgoCD CR has an empty spec.namespaceManagement. What is wrong?
expectations: States that NamespaceManagement is a handshake and that one side alone leaves the grant incomplete

Reads status.conditions on the NamespaceManagement CR, and uses it as the discriminator: an ErrorOccurred condition saying the namespace is not permitted based on NamespaceManagement rules means the feature is enabled and the ArgoCD CR is the missing side, while no condition at all points at the operator environment. Asserting that the CR reports nothing fails this expectation
Requires ArgoCD.spec.namespaceManagement to allow the namespace with both name and allowManagedBy true

Requires ALLOW_NAMESPACE_MANAGEMENT_IN_NAMESPACE_SCOPED_INSTANCES to be true, says the feature is off by default, and reads it from the operator Deployment rather than only from Subscription.spec.config.env
States that a completed handshake is what makes the operator create the Role and RoleBinding, so the user should not create them
Notes that spec.managedBy must be the Argo CD instance namespace

evals.name: Cluster-scoped resource on a namespace-scoped instance
evals.prompt: Our namespace-scoped Argo CD in team-frontend manages payments-dev. The namespace is labeled argocd.argoproj.io/managed-by=team-frontend and the Role team-argocd-argocd-application-controller exists. Sync of a ClusterRole still fails with forbidden. Do we need another managed-by label?
expectations: States that the managed-by grant is already in place because the label matches and the operator Role exists
States that a namespace-scoped instance cannot manage cluster-scoped resources such as ClusterRole, even when managed-by is set
Does not recommend another label, a hand-written ClusterRoleBinding, or elevating the tenant instance to cluster-admin

evals.name: managed-by-cluster-argocd is not destination RBAC
evals.prompt: Destination namespace payments-dev has label argocd.argoproj.io/managed-by-cluster-argocd=team-frontend and no argocd.argoproj.io/managed-by label. The Application sync into payments-dev is forbidden. Someone said that label means the GitOps operator already granted RBAC. Is that right?
expectations: States that argocd.argoproj.io/managed-by-cluster-argocd is the apps-in-any-namespace or sourceNamespaces label, not the destination-namespace grant
States that the destination grant is argocd.argoproj.io/managed-by set to the instance namespace, or a completed NamespaceManagement handshake
Does not treat managed-by-cluster-argocd as permission for the application controller to deploy workloads
Does not recommend creating a Role or RoleBinding by hand as the substitute

evals.name: AppProject rejects a destination the operator already granted
evals.prompt: Application checkout destinations to namespace checkout-prod. The namespace is labeled argocd.argoproj.io/managed-by=team-frontend. Role and RoleBinding team-argocd-argocd-application-controller exist there and oc auth can-i create deployment as system:serviceaccount:team-frontend:team-argocd-argocd-application-controller in checkout-prod returns yes. The AppProject team-checkout destinations list only namespace checkout-dev. Sync says the destination is not permitted. What is the cause?
expectations: States that the operator destination grant is present and that Kubernetes RBAC allows the controller ServiceAccount
Identifies AppProject team-checkout spec.destinations as the rejection, because checkout-prod is not listed and checkout-dev is
Does not recommend a Role, RoleBinding, or managed-by change
Does not recommend switching the Application to the default project

evals.name: Remote cluster destination
evals.prompt: Application edge syncs to server https://api.remote.example.com:6443, namespace factory. We labeled factory on the hub with argocd.argoproj.io/managed-by=team-frontend. The remote sync is still forbidden. Why did the GitOps operator not create the RBAC?
expectations: States that argocd.argoproj.io/managed-by only applies to namespaces on the same cluster as the GitOps operator
States that a remote cluster destination needs its permissions created on that remote cluster
Does not claim the hub label should have created a Role in the remote namespace

evals.name: Application in a tenant namespace is ignored entirely
evals.prompt: I created Application checkout in namespace team-payments. kubectl get application checkout -n team-payments returns the object but status is completely empty — no sync status, no health, no conditions. It never appears in the Argo CD UI. The instance is openshift-gitops, installed by the OpenShift GitOps operator. What is wrong?
expectations: Identifies the empty .status as the signature that the instance is not watching that namespace, rather than a sync, RBAC, or AppProject failure

States that the fix is .spec.sourceNamespaces on the ArgoCD CR, and that the operator derives the managed-by-cluster-argocd label, the Role and RoleBinding on applications.argoproj.io, and the --application-namespaces arguments from it
Does not recommend setting the argocd.argoproj.io/managed-by-cluster-argocd label by hand, writing a Role or RoleBinding, or editing --application-namespaces on the Deployment or StatefulSet
Also checks the AppProject's own spec.sourceNamespaces, noting that the default project does not permit other namespaces out of the box
Notes that the destination namespace grant is a separate question, so fixing sourceNamespaces alone may move the symptom from ignored to forbidden

evals.name: InvalidSpecError distinguishes the AppProject layer from the instance layer
evals.prompt: Application orders in namespace team-orders has a status, and one condition: InvalidSpecError, 'Application is not allowed in namespace team-orders'. team-orders is already listed in ArgoCD.spec.sourceNamespaces. Why is it still failing?
expectations: States that because the Application has a status at all, the instance is watching the namespace and the ArgoCD CR layer is already correct
Identifies the AppProject's spec.sourceNamespaces as the missing piece, not the ArgoCD CR
States that the AppProject is an ordinary Argo CD object and is not operator-owned, so editing it is a normal change that will not be reverted
Does not recommend re-adding or changing .spec.sourceNamespaces on the ArgoCD CR

evals.name: RBAC object format changes with apps-in-any-namespace
evals.prompt: After we enabled sourceNamespaces on our ArgoCD CR, a group that previously had access can still see the Applications in the openshift-gitops namespace but not the ones that moved into tenant namespaces. The rbac policy was not changed. Nothing is logging an error.
expectations: Identifies that for the applications resource the policy object becomes <project>/<namespace>/<application> when sourceNamespaces is in use, instead of <project>/<application>
Explains that existing two-part rules keep matching Applications in the instance namespace and silently stop matching the relocated ones, which is why some are visible and some are not
States that no error is reported because this is a non-match rather than a failure
Gives the fix as .spec.rbac.policy on the ArgoCD CR rather than an argocd-rbac-cm edit

evals.name: CR is already correct but was never reconciled
evals.prompt: I set .spec.sourceNamespaces on the ArgoCD CR two hours ago. kubectl get argocd shows the field is there. But the namespace still has no managed-by-cluster-argocd label and the controller still does not have --application-namespaces. Should I set the label manually to unblock the team?
expectations: Says no, and does not recommend setting the label, the RBAC, or the controller flag by hand
Recognises this as an operator fault rather than a misplaced setting: the CR field is already correct, so repeating it is not a useful recommendation
Compares .metadata.generation against .status.observedGeneration on the ArgoCD CR as the discriminating check
Checks whether the field was silently pruned on write by an operator version that does not know it, by reading the CR back
Hands off operator and OLM triage — pod restarts, CSV phase, InstallPlan, conversion webhook — to Workflow 6 in skills/gitops/argo-cluster-debug/SKILL.md

evals.name: Unattended diagnosis with denied evidence reads
evals.prompt: An unattended diagnostic job is investigating Application payments in team-frontend. Use the captured observations in tests/argo-cluster-debug/offline-runtime/denied-reads.json. This is an offline replay: no live cluster is available, and the snapshot includes all accessible evidence from this run. Produce the diagnosis now.
expectations: Completes a structured diagnosis without asking the user a question, requesting access, or waiting for input.
Reports Degraded health with Synced sync status and the observed Deployment ProgressDeadlineExceeded condition; does not call the sync operation failed.
Explicitly identifies the denied pod and pod-log reads as unavailable evidence for the diagnostics reader, not proof that the Argo CD controller lacks deployment permissions.
Does not invent CrashLoopBackOff, OOM, an image error, or any other underlying pod cause; states that the workload root cause remains unverified.
Reports Low confidence for the unresolved underlying cause (it may separately give high confidence in the observed rollout failure) and names the missing pod state/log evidence.
Does not execute or claim to have executed remediation, and does not re-run a full installation survey already completed in the current-run snapshot.

evals.name: Caller schema overrides runtime-specific output defaults
evals.prompt: Automated diagnosis: Application legacy-erp in team-frontend has been OutOfSync for six days. Use only the captured observations in tests/argo-cluster-debug/offline-runtime/manual-sync.json; this is an offline replay. The calling runtime requires the final answer to be one JSON object matching tests/argo-cluster-debug/offline-runtime/caller-schema.json, with no Markdown fence or surrounding prose. Produce the diagnostic result.
expectations: Final answer parses as JSON and validates against caller-schema.json, including its boolean actionRequired, lowercase confidence enum and prohibition on extra properties.
Sets actionRequired to the JSON boolean false and recommendations to an empty array.
Explains that automated sync is absent and the controller log explicitly skipped auto-sync; separates Healthy health and the prior Succeeded operation from current OutOfSync.
Does not add AnalysisResult diagnosis nesting, string True/False values, remediationPlan, RBAC declarations, or completion-state fields absent from the caller schema.
Does not ask questions, enable auto-sync, run a sync, or invent a remediation for the manual-sync policy.

evals.name: Mixed sync and health symptoms retain both causal chains
evals.prompt: Application payments in team-frontend is OutOfSync and Degraded. The sync reports forbidden, and the team also reports a crashing Deployment. Diagnose the complete incident from tests/argo-cluster-debug/offline-runtime/mixed-symptoms.json. This is an unattended offline replay; use the captured evidence and do not contact a live cluster.
expectations: Investigates the forbidden sync through operator destination-permission checks and retains the independent workload-health finding; the report contains both causal chains.

Establishes the team-frontend/team-argocd instance is namespace-scoped from operator configuration and absent instance ClusterRole, and identifies missing destination grant from namespace labels, NamespaceManagement list, destination RBAC and can-i evidence.
Separately identifies the payments Deployment crash caused by DB_PORT=not-a-number, supported by the previous container log, nonzero exit code and the matching desired manifest.
Does not claim that granting destination access fixes the DB_PORT crash, or that the crash caused Kubernetes authorization to deny Service creation.
Proposes the operator-owned destination grant rather than hand-written generated Roles/RoleBindings, and a Git correction for DB_PORT rather than a live Deployment edit that selfHeal would revert.
States the scope/impact of both recommendations, keeps Application namespace team-frontend distinct from destination payments-dev, and completes without questions or writes.
Reuses the current-run installation evidence and handoff evidence instead of restarting the generic workflow or dropping the secondary fault.

evals.name: Repeated tool calls in fresh shell sessions
evals.prompt: An unattended check found Application legacy-erp in team-frontend OutOfSync. Diagnose it using the offline cluster simulator. No live cluster may be contacted. Execute shell calls through python3 tests/argo-cluster-debug/offline-runtime/fresh-shell.py --log /tmp/argo-cluster-debug-e44.jsonl --command '<shell command>'. Each invocation starts a fresh shell with KCTL, NS, CR, APP and APP_NS unset. Use at least two separate invocations because this runtime collects Application state and controller logs in separate calls. The simulator exposes oc and kubectl: config current-context; api-resources; get applications.argoproj.io <name> -n <namespace> -o json; get argocd -A -o json; and logs statefulset/<controller> -n <namespace> --tail=50. Installation health was verified earlier in this run: team-frontend/team-argocd components are Ready, the operator CSV is Succeeded, and this is the owning instance. Read SKILL.md/references as needed; obtain diagnostic evidence through the simulator rather than reading its backing fixture.
expectations: The tool trace contains at least two separate fresh-shell.py invocations, including a successful Application read and controller-log read; merely proposing commands is a failure.

Each invocation that uses KCTL, NS, CR, APP or APP_NS defines them in that invocation, or uses explicit CLI/resource/namespace arguments; no read fails because a previous shell variable was assumed to persist.
Uses applications.argoproj.io and queries the specified Application in team-frontend without substituting another resource or instance.
Uses the observed absence of automated policy and controller log to diagnose manual sync awaiting intentional action; reports no action required and cites actual simulator output.
Completes without questions or live-cluster calls and performs no mutation; the simulator transcript contains only permitted read operations.
